newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila o/night rates steady, T-bills active.
newsitem.headline: Manila o/night rates steady, T-bills active.

text.p: Philippine overnight money was unchanged at 13.03125 percent despite higher turnover spurred by the usual weekend covering, traders said.
A total of 18.826 billion pesos changed hands on Monday compared with 12.328 billion on Friday. Done rates were wedged between 13.03125 and 13.25 percent.

While the interbank market was quiet, the secondary Treasury bill market was swamped with sellers offering higher yields in anticipation of a correction in the T-bill rates at this afternoon's auction.
"Many traders were expecting a correction today. The yield curve is already flattish," one trader said.
Three-month, six-month and one-year T-bill rates have bunched up between the 10.00 and 11.00 percent range last week.
Traders said they expected the one-year to nudge up by as much as 20 basis points, while the six-months by 10 basis points.
The benchmark 91-day T-bill rates were projected to stay sideways or slightly higher due to excess liquidity in the market.
Another trader said some banks were interpreting the higher dollar selling rate of the Central Bank in recent days to mean the Bank was mopping up pesos from the market.
The Central Bank raised its dollar selling rate to 26.385 on Friday from 26.375 earlier in the week.
Offered rates for one-year bills in the secondary market went up above the 11.0 percent level, with done deals at 11.05 percent, a survey of eight banks showed.
